summary: Birth on Sunday, the day of Sun. Jataka Bharanam describes the native as harsh in manner, little or thin hair, victorious at the front of a fight.
common_outcomes: victorious at the front of a fight
generous, brave and full of vitality
lagna_or_context_notes: A weekday is reckoned from sunrise to sunrise, so a birth before local sunrise belongs to the previous weekday (PVR sec. 1.3.11).

source_views.source: Jataka Bharanam of Dhundiraja (1800 Jammu manuscript, partial; Source Library AI translation, unreviewed, checked against the Sanskrit on the page), vara-phala v.1 (p.21)
source_views.view: Birth on Sunday (Sun's day): harsh in manner; little or thin hair; victorious at the front of a fight; strong hands; prone to bursts of anger; generous, brave and full of vitality.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach (author-hosted PDF), sec. 1.3.8-1.3.12 (sec. 1.3.11 Hora)
source_views.view: The weekday is ruled by Sun, which also rules the first hora (hour) after sunrise; the day runs sunrise to sunrise.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Lessons on Vedic Astrology vol. I (student-compiled class notes, author-hosted), lessons on panchanga (via student notes)
source_views.view: Vara belongs to the fire (agni) element and shows physical vitality; the lord of the weekday (vaaradhipati) matters for it.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, 'Panchanga Intro' (srath.com)
source_views.view: Vara is the solar limb of time: ruled by Surya, element Agni (fire).

disagreements: Only Jataka Bharanam gives birth results per weekday among the sources read; the modern sources (PVR, Rath) describe what the vara limb signifies (vitality, fire element) but give no per-day personality readings.
phrasing_guidance: One sentence at most, as a flavour of the weekday lord. Avoid physical-appearance claims (hair, build, ageing) and never present Saturday birth as unlucky; frame it as a serious, enduring temperament.
